people: Detect people, associate IDs with MOT and count directional line crossings. Validate event recall, hourly false alerts, occlusion and crossing traffic; IDs do not establish identity.
inspection: Capture a stopped or triggered workpiece and locate defects for review. Specify defect pixels, lighting and cycle deadline. Improve optics or tile images before buying more compute.
document: Rectify perspective, run text detection and recognition, then validate field formats. Add VLM only for open semantics or complex layout. Measure field accuracy and exception handling.
points: Track selected texture points and occlusion on deformable surfaces. Fix causal TAPIR, point count, input size, speed and feature pixels. High camera FPS reduces inter-frame movement but is not a universal requirement.
depthscene: Estimate foreground/background relations in warehouses, drones or mobile robots. Relative depth is not metres. Metric use requires calibration, a suitable checkpoint and ground truth.
maskscene: Select an object, propagate masks with SAM 2 and review failures. Live use needs memory-state, occlusion, restart and end-to-end latency measurements.
semantic: A light detector selects inspection frames for VLM review. Keep fast alerts on deterministic rules. Specify structured output, abstention and error acceptance.
obstacle: Fuse metric depth and odometry for low obstacles in an AMR path. Specify near/far errors, minimum obstacle size and reflective/textureless failures. Validate AI and safety controls separately.
gimbaltrack: Separate target motion from camera rotation. A gimbal does not eliminate shake. Validate timestamps, IMU alignment, shutter readout, exposure and compensation residuals.
voiceagent: A maintenance assistant retrieves manuals and proposes tool actions for confirmation. Define 500 ms as first audio or completed reply; specify model, context, endpointing, noise and echo cancellation.
ragagent: Retrieve maintenance documents and return verifiable instructions. Require citations, refusal on missing evidence, tool permissions and timeouts. Indexes also consume RAM and SSD.
checkout: Compare visible tray or package items against an order. Similar packaging, reflections, overlap and unknown SKUs require explicit validation and human review.
security: Rectify optics and run regional intrusion or person/vehicle rules. Verify low light, fisheye distortion, encoding and operating temperature; ISP integration matters.
pose: Estimate skeletal joints and classify workstation actions. Specify joint error, occlusion, people count and window latency. Skeleton data can still be sensitive.
uavtrack: Track a distant target from a drone with a narrow FOV. Estimate target pixels from range, size and optics; measure vibration, haze, heat shimmer and tracker input cadence.
uavmap: Map from aerial imagery with VIO/SLAM and GNSS or surveyed control points. Validate overlap, altitude, timestamp alignment and scale drift; relative depth alone does not provide metric mapping.
uavavoid: Use synchronized metric sensing for low-speed indoor flight. Specify obstacle size, range error, flight velocity, control delay and emergency behavior. Planning calculations are not flight certification.
mobilerobot: Combine obstacle sensing and localization on a moving robot. Validate changing viewpoints, low texture, reflective objects, IMU synchronization and minimum reliable sensing range.
vehicle: Observe distant objects from a vehicle, with detector and motion/depth paths as required. Define projected pixels, road vibration, rolling shutter and latency. This tool does not certify autonomous driving.
yolo: Start with YOLOv8 n/s/m at 640 and MOT such as ByteTrack. Inspect Conv, Resize, Concat, decode, NMS and INT8 calibration in the actual exported graph. Do not mix model generations or export recipes.
ocr: Detection and recognition are separate tasks. Text crop count adds work; validate viewing angle, glare, character pixels and business formats.
tapir: Fix causal checkpoint, points, size and state. Inspect correlation, sampling and temporal operations in the exported graph. GPU prototyping does not guarantee edge real time.
cotracker: Online mode processes chunks/windows, adding waiting time. Point count, attention and state affect memory and latency. Selected model cards run together; remove TAPIR to compare alternatives.
sam: Profile encoder, prompt decoder and memory attention separately. Paper results on A100 cannot be converted directly into Jetson or NPU FPS.
depth: DAC follows the user's Depth Anything interpretation. Separate relative and metric models. Check Resize, normalization, attention and output scale against calibration data.
vlm: Fix image tokens, context, quantization and reply length. Measure prefill, first token, complete reply and peak memory rather than borrowing detector FPS.
jev: In this tool Jev means the user's local RLCD + Qwen decision checkpoint. Specify parameters, quantization, runtime and state. Cloud API removes this model's local inference load; network and service latency still matter.
stereo: Focal length, baseline, synchronization and sensing uncertainty determine metric accuracy. Validate both processing load and physical sensor integration.
stabilize: Use calibration, IMU, global motion or optical flow to estimate camera motion. Validate rolling shutter and timestamp error; compensation is not assumed perfect.
llm: Default to the Strata Qwen3.8-Flash-Next route: GPU expert cache, CPU/RAM experts and SSD embeddings. Desktop results are not Jetson benchmarks. Cloud deployment is available separately.
asr: Specify language, microphone range, noise, wake word and endpointing. Measure WER and final-transcript latency.
tts: Specify first audio delay, language, voice and stream format. Echo cancellation and barge-in require an actual audio-loop test.
rag: Budget embeddings, reranking, indexes and tool execution separately. LLM decode tok/s alone does not describe agent latency.
posemodel: Start with lightweight pose, then choose action windows against deadlines. People count, joints, viewpoints and temporal state add load.
slam: Specify sensor calibration, timestamps, feature quality, map storage and GNSS/control-point anchors. Validate tracking loss and recovery on the actual trajectory.
realtime: Validate FPS, P95 latency, oldest frame age and drop rate together. Pipeline throughput and per-result latency are distinct.
batch: Allow processing time to trade for quality, but specify batch deadline, storage and cost. Split live and batch outputs into separate pipelines if both are needed.
private: All required inference must deploy locally. A required cloud API conflicts with this condition. Offline batch and fully offline deployment are different requirements.
power: Include compute module, carrier, cameras, storage and cooling. Module power mode is not measured system power; unknown boards remain unverified.
camera: Use actual camera FPS, image-plane speed, exposure and resized features. Frame interpolation cannot restore unobserved camera information.
multi: Streams multiply decode, ISP, transfers, model state and inference work. Verify carrier CSI/USB/Ethernet interfaces, synchronization and drivers.
fanless: Fanless operation is a complete thermal design. Test enclosure, ambient temperature and sustained workload on hardware.
memory: Set a maximum acceptable installed-memory configuration. Available memory is smaller; loading one model does not prove concurrent, long-running operation avoids OOM.
latency: Include exposure, queues, transfers, inference and postprocessing. A single-model benchmark is insufficient.
optics: Specify horizontal FOV, sensor output, target box and resized size. Wide FOV reduces pixel density; digital enlargement adds no optical detail.
motion: Estimate central image movement from FOV and angular speed, then verify timestamps, IMU alignment and shutter readout. Measure compensation residuals.
metric: Specify absolute error at near and far test points, plus percentile or maximum-error acceptance. The requirement is not proof a model achieves it.
stopping: Combine speed, P95 delay, deceleration, error and margin to estimate minimum sensing range. Validate controller and hardware behavior separately.
audio: Budget VAD, ASR, prefill, LLM, tools and TTS. Distinguish first audio from complete reply and include playback time when appropriate.
localstack: Choose model and runtime together with quantization, context, concurrency, RAM/VRAM, SSD and supported architecture.
lighting: Improve illumination and optics before increasing compute. Build acceptance data for transparent/reflective materials and occlusion.
sensorio: Check actual carrier wiring, drivers, timestamps and sustained bandwidth. SoC capability does not guarantee a board exposes it.
longrange: Combine range, target size, FOV, exposure, haze and stabilization. Small distant targets may fail at image acquisition before compute becomes the bottleneck.
iotlocal: An ESP32-S3 voice terminal captures audio, displays replies and controls devices through a local Qwen server on the home LAN. Qwen weights reside on the host. Budget concurrent ASR, LLM and TTS there. Separate BLE provisioning from audio transport; NX/AGX suitability depends on model, precision, context and concurrency.
iotcv: The camera node segments colors, detects changes or uses ESPDet-Pico for single-class detection and sends compact events. S3 uses DVP or bandwidth-limited USB UVC. P4 adds MIPI CSI/ISP and USB HS, with a separate wireless chip. Running YOLO11/YOLO26 does not imply 30 FPS; pin quantization, input, dataset and SDK.
iotcompanion: A small expressive display gadget accepts push-to-talk input, shows replies and controls home devices; compare Muse service with a self-hosted local backend. Muse requires app pairing and an SDK token; board features vary. Default replies are text; spoken output needs an added TTS integration. The local backend is a custom alternative, not an offline Muse deployment.
iotlink: The endpoint handles provisioning, audio buffers, display and control. LLM inference belongs to the chosen local or service host. Test reconnects, API permissions, OTA and rollback.
mcuvision: Start with grayscale, thresholds, color blobs or frame differences. Neural detection needs an ESP-DL-compatible quantized graph and separate SRAM, PSRAM and flash budgets. Custom YOLOv8n exports do not inherit Pico FPS.
